questions.stem: In a controlled chain reaction in a nuclear reactor, on average how many neutrons from each fission event go on to cause further fission?
questions.explanation: In a controlled chain reaction, exactly one neutron from each fission event goes on to cause another fission. This keeps the reaction rate constant. If more than one neutron caused further fission, the reaction would accelerate (uncontrolled). Control rods absorb excess neutrons to maintain this balance.

questions.stem: What is the function of control rods in a nuclear reactor?

options.text: To absorb neutrons and control the rate of the chain reaction
To transfer heat to the coolant

questions.explanation: Control rods are made of materials that absorb neutrons (such as boron or cadmium). By raising or lowering the control rods into the reactor core, operators can control how many neutrons are available to cause further fission, thereby controlling the rate of the chain reaction and the power output.
